courseCardsSection.title: Choose the right Get Ready Cohort
courseCardsSection.intro: Both cohorts are aligned to the early Integrated Math sequence used by DUSD and PUSD pathways. Students focus on the first-quarter concepts that most often create gaps when the school year begins.

im1.title: IM1 Get Ready
im1.headline: Start IM1 with strong algebra habits before the pace picks up.
im1.subheadline: A focused 4-week summer cohort for students entering DUSD or PUSD Integrated Math 1. Students strengthen the first-quarter foundations: expressions, equations, real-number properties, proportional reasoning, formulas, and early function readiness.
positioningLines: This is a first-quarter readiness cohort, not a full-year IM1 course.
Quarter 2 and beyond continue through regular tutoring.
The cohort prepares students for the early IM1 topics that often create the first major gaps.

im2.title: IM2 Get Ready
im2.headline: Move into IM2 ready for geometry reasoning, proof, and similarity.
im2.subheadline: A focused 4-week summer cohort for students entering DUSD or PUSD Integrated Math 2. Students strengthen the first-quarter foundations: triangle congruence, triangle relationships, quadrilaterals, similarity, proportional reasoning, and early right-triangle readiness.
positioningLines: This is a first-quarter readiness cohort, not a full-year IM2 course.
Quarter 2 and beyond continue through regular tutoring.
The cohort prepares students for the early IM2 topics that often create the first major geometry and proof gaps.

curriculumAlignment.title: Aligned to early IM1 readiness.
curriculumAlignment.copy: The IM1 Get Ready Cohort focuses on the skills students need before and during the first quarter of Integrated Math 1. We emphasize Module 1 and Module 2 foundations first, then build a bridge toward relations, functions, slope, and graphing so students are ready when the course begins moving faster.

cards.title: Expressions
cards.text: Students review numerical expressions, algebraic expressions, real-number properties, distributive property, absolute value expressions, and accuracy in mathematical modeling.

cards.title: Equations
cards.text: Students practice writing, interpreting, and solving equations, including one-step equations, multi-step equations, variables on both sides, absolute value equations, proportions, and formulas.

cards.title: Function Readiness
cards.text: Students build early confidence with tables, coordinate graphs, rate of change, slope, linear relationships, and the vocabulary needed for functions.

diagnosticMethod.title: We do more than review.
diagnosticMethod.subtitle: We find the mistake pattern behind the wrong answer.

features.title: Diagnose
features.text: Students solve targeted problems that show whether the issue is a small slip, a repeated procedure error, or a deeper concept gap.

features.title: Repair
features.text: We reteach the missing idea using models, examples, and guided reasoning instead of asking students to memorize another shortcut.

features.title: Strengthen
features.text: Students practice varied problems so they can transfer the skill to new questions, word problems, graphs, and tests.

whyThisMatters.title: Why IM1 gaps show up early
whyThisMatters.copy: IM1 moves quickly from arithmetic into algebraic structure. A student may understand basic operations but still struggle when expressions, variables, equations, proportions, formulas, and graphs appear together. This cohort helps students build the habits they need before those gaps become harder to fix.

weeks.title: Week 1 — Expressions and Algebraic Structure
weeks.text: Order of operations, variables, terms, coefficients, real-number properties, distributive property, and combining like terms.

weeks.title: Week 2 — Equations and Balance
weeks.text: One-step equations, multi-step equations, equations with variables on both sides, and clean step-by-step solving habits.

weeks.title: Week 3 — Absolute Value, Proportions, and Formulas
weeks.text: Absolute value expressions and equations, proportional reasoning, formula use, and interpreting what each quantity means.

weeks.title: Week 4 — Function and Graphing Readiness
weeks.text: Coordinate-plane review, tables, rate of change, slope, slope-intercept readiness, and interpreting linear relationships.

regularTutoring.title: After the cohort
regularTutoring.copy: The Get Ready Cohort is designed for first-quarter readiness. Students who want continued support for Quarter 2, homework, quizzes, tests, and long-term gap repair can continue into regular DUSD and PUSD-aligned tutoring.

faq.question: Is this a full IM1 course?
faq.answer: No. This is a focused first-quarter readiness cohort. It prepares students for the early IM1 foundations and builds readiness for functions and graphing.

faq.question: Which topics are emphasized most?
faq.answer: The main focus is expressions, equations, properties, distributive property, absolute value, proportions, formulas, and early function readiness.

faq.question: Is this for DUSD and PUSD students?
faq.answer: Yes. The cohort is designed around DUSD and PUSD Integrated Math 1 readiness needs.

faq.question: What if my child already knows some of these topics?
faq.answer: The cohort uses diagnostic practice. Students who know the basics are pushed into deeper reasoning, multi-step work, error analysis, and application problems.

faq.question: What happens after the cohort?
faq.answer: Students may continue into regular tutoring for Quarter 2 and beyond. Summer cohort families who continue into a 6-month regular tutoring plan may be eligible for up to $120 total savings.

curriculumAlignment.title: Aligned to first-quarter IM2 readiness.
curriculumAlignment.copy: The IM2 Get Ready Cohort focuses on the geometry and reasoning skills students need at the start of Integrated Math 2. We begin with the triangle congruence skills students are expected to bring from IM1, then build into triangle relationships, quadrilaterals, similarity, and early right-triangle readiness.

cards.title: Triangle Congruence Bridge
cards.text: Students review triangle angle relationships, congruent triangles, SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, right triangle congruence, isosceles and equilateral triangles, and coordinate proof readiness.

cards.title: Triangle Relationships
cards.text: Students build reasoning with perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors, medians, altitudes, triangle inequalities, indirect proof, and relationships within and between triangles.

cards.title: Quadrilaterals and Proof
cards.text: Students strengthen properties of parallelograms, rectangles, rhombi, squares, trapezoids, and kites while practicing how to justify conclusions from definitions and theorems.

cards.title: Similarity and Right-Triangle Readiness
cards.text: Students connect dilations, scale factor, similar polygons, similar triangles, triangle proportionality, and early right-triangle tools such as the Pythagorean Theorem.

diagnosticMethod.title: We do more than review geometry.
diagnosticMethod.subtitle: We find the reasoning mistake behind the wrong answer.

features.title: Diagnose
features.text: Students solve targeted geometry problems that reveal whether the issue is vocabulary confusion, theorem misuse, weak diagram interpretation, or a deeper proof gap.

features.title: Repair
features.text: We reteach the missing idea using diagrams, marked figures, theorem comparisons, and guided reasoning.

features.title: Strengthen
features.text: Students practice varied problems so they can transfer the reasoning to new diagrams, proofs, similarity problems, and tests.

whyThisMatters.title: Why IM2 gaps show up early
whyThisMatters.copy: IM2 begins with geometry reasoning. Students are no longer just finding an answer — they must justify why the answer is true. A student may know formulas but still struggle when a problem asks for proof, theorem selection, similarity reasoning, or diagram interpretation. This cohort helps students build those habits before school pace increases.
habits: Identify what is given versus what only looks true

weeks.title: Week 1 — Triangle Congruence Bridge
weeks.text: Angles of triangles, congruent triangles, SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, right triangle congruence, isosceles and equilateral triangle reasoning, and coordinate proof readiness.

weeks.title: Week 2 — Relationships in Triangles
weeks.text: Perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors, medians, altitudes, triangle inequalities, indirect proof, and reasoning about relationships inside triangles.

weeks.title: Week 3 — Quadrilaterals and Justification
weeks.text: Angles of polygons, parallelograms, tests for parallelograms, rectangles, rhombi, squares, trapezoids, kites, and coordinate-plane classification.

weeks.title: Week 4 — Similarity and Right-Triangle Readiness
weeks.text: Dilations, scale factor, similar polygons, AA/SSS/SAS similarity, triangle proportionality, parts of similar triangles, and preview of Pythagorean and special right-triangle reasoning.

faq.question: Is this a full IM2 course?
faq.answer: No. This is a focused first-quarter readiness cohort. It prepares students for the early IM2 geometry and similarity foundations and previews the right-triangle tools that appear next.

faq.question: Which topics are emphasized most?

faq.question: Why do you include triangle congruence if IM2 starts with triangle relationships?
faq.answer: Many students need a bridge from IM1 triangle congruence into IM2 geometry reasoning. Congruence, theorem selection, and proof habits support the early IM2 units.

faq.question: Is this for DUSD and PUSD students?

faq.question: What if my child already knows some geometry?
faq.answer: The cohort uses diagnostic practice. Students who know the basics are pushed into proof reasoning, diagram interpretation, similarity applications, and error analysis.

faq.question: What happens after the cohort?

curriculumAlignment.title: Built around what students see first.
curriculumAlignment.intro: The Get Ready Cohorts focus on the first-quarter concepts students are most likely to encounter early in IM1 and IM2. The goal is not to rush through the entire year. The goal is to build confidence, prevent early gaps, and strengthen the reasoning habits students need before the pace increases.

im1.title: IM1 First-Quarter Readiness
im1.copy: For students entering IM1, we focus on algebra foundations and function readiness. Students strengthen their understanding of expressions, equations, relations, functions, slope, rate of change, tables, graphs, and linear modeling.
topics: Translating real situations into algebraic models

im2.title: IM2 First-Quarter Readiness
im2.copy: For students entering IM2, we focus on geometry reasoning and similarity. Students build comfort with diagrams, theorem selection, proof structure, triangle relationships, quadrilateral properties, dilations, scale factor, and proportional reasoning.

diagnosticMethod.title: We do more than review topics.
diagnosticMethod.subtitle: GrowWise uses diagnostic practice to find the mistake patterns behind wrong answers.

features.title: Diagnose
features.text: Students work through carefully designed problems that reveal whether the issue is a slip, a repeated procedure error, or a deeper concept gap.

features.title: Repair
features.text: We reteach the missing idea using clear models, guided practice, and step-by-step reasoning.

features.title: Strengthen
features.text: Students practice similar but varied questions so they can transfer the skill instead of memorizing one pattern.

mistakePatterns.title: Common gaps we target before school starts
mistakePatterns.intro: Many students do not struggle because they are "bad at math." They struggle because one small misunderstanding becomes a repeated pattern. The cohort is designed to catch those patterns early.
im1Patterns: Misreading variables as labels instead of quantities
Treating slope as just a formula instead of a rate of change
Graphing without connecting the graph to the equation
Translating word problems too literally instead of modeling relationships
im2Patterns: Assuming facts from a diagram without proof
Using the wrong triangle or quadrilateral theorem
Applying scale factor to the wrong measurement
Solving geometry problems by calculation only without justification

steps.title: Week 1 — Baseline and Foundations

steps.title: Week 2 — Guided Skill Building
steps.text: Students work through structured examples, visual models, and teacher-led reasoning practice.

steps.title: Week 3 — Diagnostic Practice
steps.text: Students solve varied problems designed to reveal common mistakes and strengthen transfer.

steps.title: Week 4 — Readiness Review
steps.text: Students complete mixed practice, review high-risk gaps, and prepare for the first weeks of school.

faq.question: Is this a full IM1 or IM2 course?
faq.answer: No. The Get Ready Cohort is focused on first-quarter readiness. It helps students begin the year with stronger foundations, better reasoning habits, and fewer early gaps.

faq.question: Is Quarter 2 included?
faq.answer: Quarter 2 is not offered as a separate summer cohort. Students who want continued support can move into regular tutoring after the cohort.

faq.question: Is this aligned to DUSD and PUSD?
faq.answer: Yes. The program is designed around DUSD and PUSD Integrated Math pathways and focuses on the concepts students are likely to encounter early in IM1 or IM2.

faq.question: What if my child already knows some of the topics?
faq.answer: The cohort is diagnostic. Students who already know a topic are challenged with deeper reasoning, mixed practice, and mistake-pattern questions.

faq.question: What if my child struggles with math confidence?
faq.answer: The small-group format is designed to be supportive. We focus on clear steps, reasoning, and correcting misconceptions without making students feel judged.

faq.question: Who is eligible for the $120 savings?
faq.answer: The thank-you benefit is available only to Summer Get Ready Cohort families who continue into a 6-month regular tutoring plan. Eligible families may receive up to $120 total savings.

faq.question: Can my child join regular tutoring without joining the cohort?
faq.answer: Yes. Regular tutoring is available separately. The summer cohort thank-you benefit, however, is reserved for cohort families.
